text:
nina: quick sync: we need a graceful pattern for resident-tenants when cross-region failover is forbidden but the local model is unavailable or busy. customer complained that failover returned 503s and they lost UX.
omar: problem is we can't move weights for resident tenants. options: block+error, wait, or return degraded content.
kevin: idea: "local-shadow" fallback — run a distilled, small in-region model that approximates the primary. If present, proxy will return that immediately with a clear degraded header and telemetry. If not present, proxy can kick off an async cross-region job that requires explicit tenant opt-in and will deliver a callback when complete.
li: neat. two paths: (A) synchronous distilled fallback (fast, cheaper, possibly lower quality), (B) async full-quality retrieval (slower, requires consent). Both respect residency.
sara: Implementation details: 1) manifest needs `fallback_profile` listing available in-region standby models (ids + quality_tier). 2) proxy preflight decides: if tenant.residency.enforced and candidate.region != resident_region then consult fallback_profile. 3) if distilled available -> route to distilled runtime path and add header `X-Redwood-Degraded: local_shadow;quality=tier-2` and telemetry `failover.used.local_shadow`. 4) if not available but tenant has opt-in flag `allow_deferred_cross_region` -> start deferred job: store request, route to cross-region service that will run full model and post results to callback endpoint, and return synchronous response `202` with `Location: /deferred/result/{id}`.
omar: need to be careful with privacy/legal: even async cross-region path must record explicit consent and audit. legal: thoughts?
legal: we can support async cross-region only with per-tenant signed opt-in, logged operator id, and retention policy. Provide a dashboard toggle + per-request ephemeral consent token that the SDK frontend can prompt the user to accept. Must also warn about possible data residency implications.
kevin: perf: distilled models are small (~700MB) and cold-start <300ms if pre-warmed in warm pool. For warm-pool-scarce regions we can provide a pre-warm budget for resident-critical tenants. Cost impact: pre-warm + storage.
li: fallback_profile manifest example I propose: `fallback_profile: ["gen-small-3b","embed-lite-1b"]` and a `fallback_policy` field: `priority: [local_shadow, deferred_cross_region, block]`, `max_async_wait_seconds: 300`.
sara: proxy pseudo: ```
meta = GET /tenant/{id}/manifest
if meta.residency.enforced and candidate.region != meta.residency.region:
  if meta.fallback_policy.priority.contains("local_shadow") and local.has_model(meta.fallback_profile[0]):
    forward_to(local_shadow)
  else if meta.fallback_policy.priority.contains("deferred_cross_region") and tenant.opt_in: 
    enqueue_deferred_request()
    return 202 + Location
  else:
    return 451 + X-Redwood-Degraded: residency_blocked
```
nina: metrics we need: `failover.local_shadow.count`, `failover.deferred.enqueued`, `deferred.completed.latency`, `deferred.denied.no_consent`. Also sample the original input (sanitized) for QA parity checks.
omar: operator playbook: - if `failover.local_shadow` spikes: consider increasing prewarm budget or promote a higher-quality distilled to region. - if `deferred.completed.latency` > SLA alert SRE. - include runbook step to notify customer with opt-in link if many deferred requests queued.
eason: ops-bot: added feature flags: `fallback.local_shadow_enabled`, `fallback.deferred_enabled`. staging default: local_shadow on, deferred off.
li: SDK change: add helper `requestDeferredConsent(callbackUrl)` which opens consent modal and requests ephemeral consent token; SDK attaches token in header `X-Redwood-Deferred-Consent`. Must record token in audit log.
sara: Security note: deferred jobs store inputs for up to `deferred_retention_seconds`; encrypt at rest using tenant-managed keys if provided. Add `deferred_storage_policy` to manifest.
legal: also need templated wording and an API contract for callbacks to customers. We'll draft consent text: "By consenting you allow Redwood to temporarily process this request in another region to provide a higher-quality result. Data will be handled per your residency settings and logged for audit."
kevin: rollout plan: 1) add manifest fields + proxy preflight (feature-flagged), 2) implement local-shadow runtime path + prewarm budget, 3) deferred queue + callback service behind flag, 4) SDK + dashboard consent flow, 5) legal + ops checklist. Pilot with a small cohort of resident tenants next month.
li: minor: return code `451` for residency blocked (unavailable for legal reasons) instead of 503 so clients can show proper message. Good practice.
nina: thanks. canary note: ops please enable `fallback.local_shadow_enabled` for staging only and seed a few distilled models into eu-west warm pool for testing.
eason: ops-bot: staging flags set; seeded `gen-small-3b` as local_shadow for eu-west warm pool.
legal: created ticket L-3412 for consent language and audit template.
kevin: I'll author RFC with manifest examples, proxy pseudo-code, sample headers, metrics, and operator runbook. ETA draft: 72h.
nina: great. End of thread.
